title: Pharmacy - Mrs Alice Ramsey
writingTask:
Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to the daughter, Mrs Holly Kerr, 3 Rose Avenue, Springbank, 
outlining her mother’s medication regime, any potential adverse effects to be aware of, and when to seek medical 
advice.
In your answer:
●
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
●
Do not use note form
●
Use letter format
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
caseNotes: An elderly patient who has been treated for a fractured femur is being discharged from Newtown Hospital.
A letter is being written to her carer (her daughter) to ensure the medication regime is followed when she returns home.
Patient name: Mrs Alice Ramsey.
Date of birth: 04 Jan 1929.
Allergies: nil.
On admission she was taking Zantac (ranitidine) for GORD: 150mg twice daily.
On admission she was taking Lipitor (atorvastatin) 20mg every morning, on an empty stomach.
The patient had been stabilised on these medications for some years.
On discharge, medication includes Zantac (ranitidine) for GORD: 150mg twice daily.
On discharge, medication includes Lipitor (atorvastatin) 20mg.

On discharge, medication includes Dalteparin (Fragmin), a low molecular weight heparin anticoagulant: 2500IU subcutaneously, to be continued until mobile; the patient has been advised on the subcutaneous administration process.
On discharge, medication includes Panadeine Forte (paracetamol and codeine) for pain relief: 500mg, every four hours as needed.
On discharge, medication includes Durolax, to prevent constipation: 10mg at night.
On discharge, medication includes Maxolon (metoclopramide) for nausea associated with codeine: 10mg, three times a day, as required.
Adverse drug reactions for Ranitidine include headache, gastrointestinal upset, rash, and rarely CNS disturbances.

Adverse drug reactions for Atorvastatin include serious reactions such as rhabdomyolysis, myopathy and myalgia (0.2%), as well as gastrointestinal upset (1%), headache (2%), rash (2.5%), flu-like symptoms (1.5%), and raised liver function tests (1.3%).
Adverse drug reactions for Heparin include haemorrhage, easy bruising, nausea and vomiting.
Adverse drug reactions for Codeine/Paracetamol include constipation, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting, and rarely dependence, tolerance and CNS disturbances including impaired alertness.
Adverse drug reactions for Metoclopramide include rare CNS disturbances such as impaired alertness, and rarely tardive dyskinesia.
The patient normally lives alone; on discharge she will be staying with her daughter.
The patient is a non-driver and uses public transport.
Height 168cm, weight 75kg, BMI 26.8.
Non-smoker.
Dentures, upper and lower.
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD), controlled by medication.
Hypercholesterolaemia, controlled by medication.
On 11 July 2018 the patient was brought to the Emergency Department by ambulance, having been knocked down by a car in a car park and having fallen on her right side onto her femur.
Presenting symptoms were pain and difficulty standing or walking.
She was seen by Dr Hogarth and given pethidine for pain relief.
X-rays of the femur were taken, with repeat films and an MRI.
She was transferred to the ward and booked for surgery on 12 July, nil by mouth from midnight.
Full pre-operative investigations were carried out.
On 12 July 2018, open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) surgery was performed.
General anaesthetic was given, with induction using propofol, and also sevoflurane, fentanyl, midazolam, suxamethonium and ondansetron.
Heparin was given during surgery for thrombus prevention.
IV antibiotic prophylaxis (cefazolin 2g IV) was given for 24 hours after surgery.
She was immobilised with a spica cast.

Post-operative care included pressure sore prevention, wound care, pain relief, fluid balance and blood loss monitoring, nutritional management with oral protein supplementation, thrombus prevention with low-dose LMWH and compression stockings, monitoring of lower limb circulation and sensation, and early mobilisation and weight-bearing on the injured leg.
On 24 July 2018 she was transferred to the Rehabilitation Unit.
On 08 August 2018 she is due for discharge home; an appointment has been made for 22 August 2018 for removal of the cast.
Heparin is to be continued only until the patient is mobile.
The patient is being discharged into the care of her daughter.
candidateLetter:
Holly Kerr
Springbank

8 August 2018

Dear Holly,

Re: Mrs Alice Ramsey

Your mother, Mrs Alice Ramsey, was knocked down by a car in a car park on 11 July 2018 and was brought to the emergency department by ambulance, where she was seen by Dr Hogarth and give pethidine for the pain. She had an operation for her broken femur on 12 July under general anaesthetic with propofol, sevoflurane, fentanyl and midazolam. She is 168cm tall and weighs 75kg, BMI 26.8. Poor thing, it has been a very hard time for her and for all of you.

Now she was discharge from Newtown Hospital and she is going to stay with you, so I just wanted to tell you some things about her tablets.

Zantac 150mg once in the morning for her reflux. Lipitor 20mg is for her cholesterol but it usually causes muscle damage. She also have Fragmin injection s/c 2500IU, which is LMWH, and she was given it because she had a blood clot in her leg. She can take Panadeine Forte (paracetamol and codeine) 500mg every four hours as needed for pain. Durolax 10mg at night. For consitpation. She has no allergies.

Side effects - headache, rash, stomach upset, reduced alertness, nausia and vomiting, dependence. Also flu-like symptoms.

Please dont worry too much about her! If anything happens, just call someone.

Best regards,

Pharmacist
